newsitem.title: USA: Dow sets record on eve of Black Monday anniversary.
newsitem.headline: Dow sets record on eve of Black Monday anniversary.

text.p: The Dow industrials reached for the 6100 level just days after topping 6000 for the first time in history as still-solid corporate earnings reports stoked buying on the eve of Black Monday's ninth anniversary.

"We have slow economic growth, inflation is not a problem and by and large, companies are hitting or beating earnings estimates," said William LeFevre, a senior market analyst at Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum.
The Dow rose 35 to a record 6094, weighed heavily by an erosion in Philip Morris shares, down 5-1/8 to 92-1/4.
Tobacco shares were hammered by news that scientists claimed they had established the first direct link on a cellular level between smoking and cancer.

But in their record run, U.S. stocks managed to sidestep the rubble in Morris and Xerox. Xerox was down 8-1/8 to 48-7/8 after reporting third quarter results of $0.68 a share that fell well short of Street expectations.
It was the Dow's 31st record closing high for 1996 and the fourth this week. The blue chip index surged about 125 points this week.It ended above 6000 for the first time on Monday.
Among other indices, the S&P 500 rose four to a record 711.
It was also the S&P 500's fourth all-time high this week.
The NYSE Composite added two to about 378, its second straight record closing high. After shedding 16 points over the past two sessions, the Nasdaq Composite was fractionally higher at about 1242.
Winners beat losers 13-10 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 468 million shares, swollen by double-witching.

"We're still in a bull market cycle that started several years ago. We may have periodic hesitations but it's not the final top yet. We may go up another 100-200 Dow points by year end,"said Merrill Lynch chief technical analyst Richard McCabe.
But he cautioned that he saw a few signs "that we're in the seventh or eighth inning of the game."
Saturday marks the ninth anniversary of Black Monday, or October 19, 1987, when the Dow plummeted 508 points or 22.61 percent.

"Here we are nine years after the event and all sorts of people remember it well. But we're up almost 250 percent from the crash or 4320 points. So yes, there may be some October jitters but hey, if 1000 points were chopped off it's still a good run," LeFevre said. "The October jitters are probably for the bears to justify their stance," he added.

Greatly aiding the Dow's advance was IBM, up 3-7/8 to 129-3/8 after Thursday's two-point drop. Big Blue is expected to report third quarter earnings on Monday and some traders were hopeful of an upside surprise. The First Call consensus is $2.43 a share. IBM earned $2.30 a share a year ago.

Among other shares, Iomega rose 1-3/16 to 24-1/16 after the desk-drive maker reported third quarter earnings that were better than Wall Street expected and announced plans to list on the NYSE, moving from Nasdaq.
Microsoft lost 3/4 to 134-3/4. SoundView Financial downgraded the software maker to a short-term hold from buy.

Vantive Corp shed 9-1/2 to 31-1/4 after reporting a rise in quarterly profits but warning that revenue growth will be flat for the next two quarters, analysts said. Vantive officials were not available for comment.

McDonald's lost 1/2 to 46 after posting quarterly results that missed the consensus by a penny. The fast food giant said its U.S. operating performance was not keeping pace with its goals and third quarter operating income fell from last year.
Weaker tobacco shares included Loews Corp, off 1-5/8 to 80, RJR Nabisco Holdings, off 3/4 to 26-3/4, and smokeless tobacco maker UST Inc, off 5/8 to 29-1/8.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.52 to 1242.48.
The S&P 500 index rose 3.83 to 710.82, a record.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
